rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told not to look with longing at worldly enjoyment granted to counterparts of those who turn away from God's signs.
rows.anchor: يتمتعون بها، من زهرة عاجل الدنيا ونضرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their attractive worldly enjoyment is a passing deception and a test by which God tries them.
rows.anchor: لنختبرهم فيما متعناهم به من ذلك، ونبتليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised afterlife reward from God is better than their worldly adornment and lasts forever without ending or depletion.
rows.anchor: وأدوم، لأنه لا انقطاع له ولا نفاذ

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi reports that the Prophet sent him to borrow food from a Jewish man, who demanded collateral; the Prophet was saddened, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رافع، قال: أرسلني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى يهودي يستسلفه، فأبى أن يعطيه إلا برهن، فحزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: In another Abu Rafi report, a Jewish lender required a pledge after a guest arrived; the Prophet offered his armor, and verses 15:87 and 20:131–132 were revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رافع، قال: نزل برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيف: فأرسلني إلى يهودي بالمدينة يستسلفه، فأتيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭabarī parses زهرة as accusative, attached to the action of granting enjoyment despite the intervening pronoun in متعنا به.
rows.anchor: أبعد الذي بالسفح سفح كواكب … رهينة رمس من تراب وجندل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a Banū Fuqʿas poem using رهينة as an accusative by an implied verb; Ṭabarī says this is weaker evidence because the noun is governed by a preposition.
rows.anchor: فنصب رهينة على الفعل من قوله: «أبعد الذي بالسفح»

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah glosses the test as trial and says the Lord's provision is better and more lasting than their worldly enjoyment.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {لنفتنهم فيه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must command his household to pray and patiently keep up prayer himself, performing it with its prescribed limits.
rows.anchor: لا نسألك مالا، بل نكلفك عملا ببدنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks the Prophet for bodily work, not wealth, promises a great reward for it, and provides wealth Himself.
rows.anchor: نحن نعطيك المال ونكسبكه، ولا نسألكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good final outcome of every person's deeds belongs to the God-fearing, not those who fear no punishment or hope for no reward.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، قال: كان عروة إذا رأى ما عند السلاطين دخل داره

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa reports that when ʿUrwa saw the rulers' worldly goods, he went home, recited these verses, and called his family to prayer.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، قال: كان عروة إذا رأى ما عند السلاطين دخل داره، فقال

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa also reports that when ʿUrwa saw something worldly, he went to his family and told them to pray.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، أنه كان إذا رأى شيئا من الدنيا جاء إلى أهله، فقال: الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People's reckoning draws near: they will be questioned about their deeds and blessings, and whether they obeyed or disobeyed God in them.
rows.anchor: إياهم ماذا عملوا فيها، وهل أطاعوه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly life they disregard the approaching reckoning, failing to reflect, prepare, or make ready because they do not grasp its severe trials and terrors.
rows.anchor: وقد أعرضوا عن ذلك، فتركوا الفكر فيه، والاستعداد له والتأهب، جهلا منهم بما هم لاقوه عند ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet explained their heedlessness as being in worldly life.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Gog and Magog are released, God's true promise of resurrection from the graves for reward and punishment draws near.
rows.anchor: والعقاب، وهو لا شك حق، كما قال جل ثناؤه

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Ḥudhayfa says that after Gog and Magog emerge, even a foal raised by a man would not be ridden before the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ثنا حذيفة: «لو أن رجلا، افتلى فلوا بعد خروج يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the true promise drawing near as the Day of Resurrection approaching them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {واقترب الوعد الحق}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭabarī treats the conjunction wāw as inserted; the intended sequence is that once Gog and Magog are released, the true promise draws near.
rows.anchor: والواو في قوله: {واقترب الوعد الحق}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares the conjunction to 37:104, understood without its wāw, and cites an Imruʾ al-Qays line with successive unjoined verbs.
rows.anchor: وذلك نظير قوله: {فلما أسلما وتله للجبين وناديناه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's poetic line uses an unjoined successive verb to illustrate the conjunction analysis.
rows.anchor: فلما أجزنا ساحة الحي وانتحى … بنا بطن خبت ذي حقاف عقنقل

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes هي refer to the eyes, with أبصار الذين كفروا clarifying it; an anonymous poem offers a similar pronoun followed by its referent.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن تكون كناية عن الأبصار

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, هي is a supporting pronoun (ʿimād), as in 22:46; Ṭabarī also adduces a poetic parallel.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون عمادا، كما قال جل ثناؤه: {فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار}

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟
يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مِّنْ هَٰذَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' lament is understood as their response to the horrors of the Hour: they now see and endure what they had ignored.
rows.anchor: وذلك (يقولون) من قوله: {فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا}

words: يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مِّنْ هَٰذَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text leaves out “they say,” which is understood from the preceding description of the disbelievers' staring eyes.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام متروك ترك ذكره استغناء بدلالة ما ذكر عليه عنه، وذلك (يقولون) من قوله

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers people disputing God without knowledge: if they doubt resurrection, their staged creation shows that restoring them after death is no harder for the One who first created them.
rows.anchor: وهذا احتجاج من الله على الذي أخبر عنه من الناس أنه يجادل في الله بغير علم، اتباعا منه للشيطان المريد

words: فَإِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recalls creating Adam from dust and then people from Adam's seed through successive stages, as evidence of His power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: فإن في ابتدائنا خلق أبيكم آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم من تراب، ثم إنشائناكم من نطفة آدم، ثم تصريفناكم أحوالا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the adjectives as describing the drop: fully formed and sound, or expelled before becoming a formed embryo.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هي من صفة النطفة. قال: ومعنى ذلك: فإنا خلقناكم من تراب، ثم من نطفة مخلقة وغير مخلقة

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that an angel asks whether the drop is formed; if so, it records sex, provision, lifespan, and destiny from the Mother of the Book; an unformed drop is expelled as blood.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: " إذا وقعت النطفة في الرحم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah explains مخلقة وغير مخلقة as complete and incomplete.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، في قول الله: {مخلقة وغير مخلقة}

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another group says the adjectives describe a mudghah shaped like a human and one not yet shaped.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك المضغة مصورة إنسانا، وغير مصورة، فإذا صورت فهي مخلقة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies formed and unformed cases as miscarried embryos, one formed and one not formed.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {مخلقة}

rows.speaker: عامر
rows.claim: ʿĀmir says a drop or embryo that reaches the fourth stage of formation is formed; one cast out earlier is unformed.
rows.anchor: عن عامر، «أنه قال في النطفة والمضغة

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya glosses the phrase as miscarriage.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية: {مخلقة وغير مخلقة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭabarī prefers fully imaged embryos as formed and miscarriage before formation is complete as unformed, when the womb expels an unshaped mudghah without ensoulment.
rows.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: المخلقة المصورة خلقا تاما، وغير مخلقة: السقط قبل تمام خلقه

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whomever God decrees to live until a fixed term is kept in the womb, neither miscarried nor delivered before the appointed time; God then permits birth.
rows.anchor: منها، فيخرج. وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses remaining in the womb until a fixed term as completion.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the appointed term is the embryo's stay in the womb until it comes out.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُتَوَفَّىٰ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some die before maturity; others live past their prime into senility, becoming like children and losing knowledge they once had.
rows.anchor: في أجله فيعمر حتى يهرم، فيرد من بعد انتهاء شبابه

words: أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oldest age means decrepitude after strength and maturity, when a person no longer understands what he previously knew.
rows.anchor: ذلك الهرم، حتى يعود كهيئته في حال صباه لا يعقل من بعد عقله الأول شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāmidah describes dry, barren land whose plant traces have disappeared; the root denotes wearing away and extinction.
rows.anchor: وأصل الهمود: الدروس والدثور

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports Mujāhid's explanation of the dormant earth as land with no vegetation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، في قوله: {وترى الأرض هامدة}

rows.speaker: الأعشى ميمون بن قيس
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā Maymūn ibn Qays uses همدا for worn-out garments, supporting Ṭabarī's sense of hamūd as wearing away.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى ميمون بن قيس: [البحر الكامل] قالت قتيلة: ما لجسمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain stirs barren land with vegetation and makes the plants grow and increase.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {اهتزت وربت}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah says the rain is recognized in the land's swelling.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {اهتزت وربت}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: In another report, Qatādah says the land becomes good and the rain is recognized in its swelling.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {اهتزت وربت}

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Some direct the sense of “stirred” to the crops, although the verse grammatically speaks about the earth.
rows.anchor: وكان بعضهم يقول: معنى ذلك: فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت. ويوجه المعنى إلى الزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Major readers have rabat, meaning growth and increase; Ṭabarī rejects Abū Jaʿfar's hamzated rabʾat as mistaken because rabʾ means guarding, which does not fit here.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو جعفر القارئ يقرأ ذلك: (وربأت) بالهمز، حدثت عن الفراء، عن أبي عبد الله التميمي، عنه. وذلك غلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dormant earth produces every kind of beautiful plant after rain; bahīj means beautiful or pleasing.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah glosses bahīj as beautiful.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج}

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do you not see” means know with the heart; heavenly beings include angels, and earthly beings include jinn and other creatures.
rows.anchor: ألم تر يا محمد بقلبك، فتعلم أن الله يسجد له من في السماوات من الملائكة، ومن في الأرض من الخلق من الجن وغيرهم

words: وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prostration is that of their shadows as the sun rises and declines and each shadow shifts.
rows.anchor: وسجود ذلك ظلاله حين تطلع عليه الشمس وحين تزول، إذا تحول ظل كل شيء، فهو سجوده

words: وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the prostration of all these things is their shadows.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السموات ومن في الأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب} قال: «ظلال هذا كله»

rows.speaker: أبو العالية الرياحي
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says every star, sun, and moon prostrates when it sets, remains so until permitted to turn right, and then returns toward its rising place.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا العالية الرياحي، يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many people who prostrate are believers in God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses the many people as believers.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many people deserve God's punishment for disbelief, while their shadows still prostrate to Him.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the condemned person still prostrates along with his shadow.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Mujāhid's reading the second كثير is coordinated with prostrating believers and حق عليه العذاب modifies it; alternatively it is an independent subject whose punishment implies refusal to prostrate.
rows.anchor: وقع قوله: {وكثير حق عليه العذاب}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If outside the prostrating group, كثير is raised by the pronoun in حق عليه; this means many refused prostration, as their punishment shows disobedience.
rows.anchor: وكان معنى الكلام حينئذ: وكثير أبى السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may abase or honor whom He wills because creation and command belong to Him; the following continuation rejects a reading opposed by the authoritative readers.
rows.anchor: إكرام، وذلك قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها لإجماع الحجة

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read مكرِم as “one who honors,” but Ṭabarī rejects this vocalization because authoritative readers agree against it.
rows.anchor: إكرام، وذلك قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها لإجماع الحجة

words: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق
rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that when the Prophet left Mecca, a man said they had expelled their Prophet; the permission-to-fight verses followed, and the expelled were Muhammad and his companions.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: " لما خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when the Prophet left Mecca, Abū Bakr feared their destruction; after permission to fight was revealed, he knew fighting would occur, and the report calls it the first verse revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq notes a difference in readers' vocalization of أذن, comparing their reading with the form at 9:61.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: كانوا يقرءون: { «أذن» } [التوبة: 61]

words: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق
rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says permission to fight was given after the believers had been spared for ten years; those expelled were the believers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا}
